knowledge:
- key_parameters: betaMatrix=A matrix of beta values where columns are samples and rows are probes ;; designInfo=A data frame containing physical chip and position information, obtained via getDesignInfo ;; backgroundInfo=A data frame containing median background intensities of green and red channels, obtained via getBackground ;; outliers.perc=Percentage of outlier samples to be trimmed in the robust regression (default is 0.02, can be set between 0 and 1) ;; goodProbes=An optional vector of probe names to restrict normalization to a subset of probes (non-normalized probes are set to NA) ;; chipCorrection=Logical indicating whether chip correction should be performed (default is TRUE; set to FALSE if chips are confounded with biological characteristics) ;; sampleNames=A vector of sample names in the format SentrixID_RowCol (e.g., 5621146023_R01C01) used to extract design info ;; positionVector=An explicit vector of position indices (1 to 12) if sample names are not in the standard format ;; chipVector=An explicit vector of chip indices if sample names are not in the standard format
- alternatives: Quantile normalization is mentioned as a popular alternative for gene expression, but the documentation argues it is inappropriate for DNA methylation data because overall methylation levels can significantly differ across biological groups (e.g., tumor vs normal, or age-related hypomethylation).
- when_to_use: Use this package when normalizing DNA methylation data from the Illumina Infinium HumanMethylation 450k assay, particularly when global methylation differences are expected across samples and standard quantile normalization assumptions do not hold.
- pitfalls: The order of samples in the beta matrix must be identical to that of the samples in the negative control probe matrices ;; If samples are allocated to chips according to biological characteristics (e.g., gender or case-control status), chip correction should not be performed (chipCorrection=FALSE) because it will remove important biological variation ;; Automatic design extraction via getDesignInfo requires sample names to follow the standard Sentrix barcode format; otherwise, explicit chip and position vectors must be manually provided.

workflows.name: arrm_normalization_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Perform Adaptive Robust Regression normalization on 450k methylation data and visualize technical artifacts.
input: betaMatrix (matrix of Beta values with samples as columns and probes as rows)
greenControlMatrix (matrix of green channel negative control probe intensities)
redControlMatrix (matrix of red channel negative control probe intensities)
workflows.stages: 1. Extract background intensities using getBackground ;; 2. Extract physical chip and position information using getDesignInfo ;; 3. Perform ARRm normalization using normalizeARRm ;; 4. Extract beta value distribution quantiles using getQuantiles ;; 5. Generate diagnostic plots for background and dye bias effects using quantilePlots ;; 6. Generate diagnostic plots for spatial position effects using positionPlots ;; 7. Extract robust regression coefficients using getCoefficients
workflows.code:
backgroundInfo <- getBackground(greenControlMatrix, redControlMatrix)
designInfo <- getDesignInfo(sampleNames)
normMatrix <- normalizeARRm(betaMatrix=betaMatrix, designInfo=designInfo, backgroundInfo=backgroundInfo, outliers.perc=0.1)
quantiles=getQuantiles(betaMatrix)
quantilePlots(quantiles, backgroundInfo, designInfo)
positionPlots(quantiles, designInfo, percentiles=c(25, 50, 75))
coefficients <- getCoefficients(quantiles, designInfo, backgroundInfo, outliers.perc=0.02)
